question.text: A Cat I/II AIF IM is comparing a 100% catch-up clause vs a 50% partial catch-up, all other terms equal. Which statement is MOST accurate from the LP's perspective?

answer.text: LPs prefer 100% catch-up because they receive hurdle faster
100% catch-up is illegal under SEBI AIF Regulations
Both have identical LP impact; only GP economics differ
LPs prefer 50% partial catch-up because more of the above-hurdle residual is shared between LP and GP, reducing the GP's share of residual profits

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 6: higher catch-up rate = more of residual profits to Manager = HIGHER risk to LPs of receiving a reduced (or zero) share of above-hurdle residual until GP reaches its catch-up target. A 50% partial catch-up LEAVES more for LPs during the catch-up layer. **The Trap:** A reverses the preference; C is false; D is false (catch-up is permitted). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests this preference logic. XIX-A from LP-side. XIX-E (Cat III) has no catch-up concept. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When pitching, lead with 100% catch-up for GP pitching and offer 50/50 as an 'LP-friendly flex'. Many Indian GPs convert anchor LPs by offering a lower hurdle (8% vs 10%) AND 100% catch-up together — model both before committing.
